rows.reasoning: Bray voted Nay on HB 1032 (2026), which would have authorized mid-decade amendment of congressional districts by the general assembly, enacted a new 2026 congressional map, and limited judicial review of apportionment challenges; the Senate defeated it 19-31. A No vote names no rung: at most it rules out the party that controls the state legislature without outside interference, and it leaves state legislatures with court oversight to prevent extreme partisan bias and the three commission rungs all unevidenced.
